raw_response:
I will stay close to what has worked for me here in Quzhou. At my age, I do not like making big changes unless I have seen them work on other people’s land. With 5 mu and only 2 people at home, I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steady road for grain, and I will leave a smaller piece for cotton so I still have some cash crop income. I have well water, so I am not as afraid of dry spells as people who wait on rain, but water and fertilizer both cost money, so I will not throw them around blindly. Still, when I am uncertain, I would rather feed the crop a bit heavier than let yield fall. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer, water it a few key times, and aim for a solid stand through winter and spring. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here that is what many people plant now and the ears are better if fertilizer and water keep up. For cotton, I will keep only a small area, manage it a little tighter, and spray more times than grain because insects can ruin it fast. I will use rotary tillage on most ground because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing every time, and for my small place that is practical.
